jobs.description:

Maven Clinic is the world's largest virtual clinic for women and families on a mission to make healthcare work for all of us. Recognized for innovation and industry leadership, Maven has been named to the TIME100 Most Influential Companies, CNBC Disruptor 50, Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies, and FORTUNE Best Places to Work. Learn more at mavenclinic.com

An award-winning culture working towards an important mission –  Maven Clinic is a recipient of over 30 workplace and innovation awards, including: 

  • TIME 100 Most Influential Companies (2023, 2026)
  • Fortune Change the World (2024)
  • CNBC Disruptor 50 List (2022, 2023, 2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces for Millennials (2024)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces in Health Care (2024)
  • Fast Company Most Innovative Companies (2020, 2023)
  • Fortune Best Workplaces NY (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

About the Role: 

As a Senior Executive Assistant, you will support four to five members of Maven’s C-suite and play an important role in helping them use their time effectively. You’ll manage complex calendars, coordinate travel and meetings, anticipate needs, and keep priorities and follow-ups moving. This role calls for strong judgment, discretion, and a calm, proactive approach. You’ll work closely with the executives you support, the broader Executive Assistant team, and partners across Maven to make sure the details are handled and leaders are prepared to focus on the work that matters most.

What you'll do:

  • Manage complex calendars and scheduling. Coordinate internal and external meetings across competing priorities, maintain clean calendars, and proactively resolve conflicts. Build in appropriate preparation, travel, and follow-up time.
  • Help executives make the best use of their time. Learn their priorities and working styles, flag calendar tradeoffs, identify meetings that may need to be delegated or reconsidered, and surface conflicts or risks early.
  • Coordinate meetings from start to finish. Prepare agendas and materials as needed, confirm attendees and logistics, and make sure meeting links, rooms, and technology are ready. Help executives prepare for high-stakes conversations and track resulting follow-ups.
  • Manage travel and expenses. Arrange door-to-door travel and accommodations, share clear itineraries and relevant materials in advance, monitor travel changes, and submit expenses promptly in line with company policy.
  • Communicate on executives’ behalf. Serve as a thoughtful point of contact for colleagues and external stakeholders. Draft and coordinate clear, concise communications that reflect each executive’s tone and priorities.
  • Support board and investor logistics. Coordinate scheduling, materials, and logistics for board meetings, investor interactions, and other external stakeholder engagements, with discretion and care. Place after “Own logistics of events and gatherings.”
  • Track work and close loops. Maintain an organized view of open tasks, deadlines, and commitments; keep executives and stakeholders informed; and make sure handoffs have clear owners and next steps. Be comfortable working cross-functionally with teams that your execs depend on.
  • Support special projects. Take ownership of selected projects that improve executive operations, team coordination, or the EA team’s shared resources. Identify and implement process improvements for your executives and the EA team.
  • Own logistics of events and gatherings. Coordinate executive and team meetings, offsites, dinners, celebrations, and other events, managing logistics and working with internal partners and vendors often on the ground.

The Stripe Marketing organization is undergoing a fundamental transformation in how it works. As a Forward Deployed AI Accelerator, you'll be embedded with a cohort of 25–45 marketers organized by functional team, shared workflow, or location. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.

As the Technical Program Manager for AI Experiences, you’ll partner with product, design, and engineering teams building native AI experiences and agents so that customers meet one connected product, not a collection of separate features. You’ll map the journeys customers take across AI features, align teams on how those journeys should feel and behave, and make experience quality visible to design and product leadership through metrics and reporting.

You will work remotely from Bulgaria and will be reporting to the Manager, Technical Program and Operations.

You Will:

  • Drive experience continuity. Maintain a view of the end-to-end customer journeys that cross multiple AI features, such as starting a task with one agent and finishing it in another. Name a single accountable owner for each journey, set decision dates, and overlay team roadmaps without replacing them.
  • Establish experience standards. Work with product and design to set shared interaction patterns and behaviors: how handoffs are presented, what context carries over, how agents identify themselves, how permissions are explained, and how errors are handled and recovered from. About Mixpanel

Mixpanel is the leading product intelligence and analytics platform, trusted by more than 29,000 companies to help understand how people use the products they build. By combining powerful analytics with AI that knows your business, Mixpanel helps teams see what’s working, diagnose what’s not, and decide what to build next. Learn more at mixpanel.com.

About the Customer Digital Experience Team

Customer Digital Experience sits within the technical arm of Mixpanel's Customer Success organization.

Our sharpest focus is the digital-only segment: thousands of companies with no proactive account coverage. Some have technical resources available to them, but that support is entirely reactive. It answers the ticket and solves the problem in front of it. Nobody is watching for the customer who implemented and then never built a report, or the account whose usage has been sliding for a month. Our job is to be proactive,, and everything we build should be as automated as possible, without a human initiating it.

Our programs run across the full customer base and are not one-size-fits-all. We build flows that branch and adapt by segment, tuning the content, timing, and channel for who's receiving them. An onboarding flow for a digital-only customer carries the whole experience; the version reaching an account with a dedicated team is tuned to complement what that team is already doing. Same underlying program, deliberately different execution, continuously optimized based on what each segment responds to.

We're close to the data and to the technical reality of how customers implement and use Mixpanel. We're not guessing at what customers are doing; we can see it, and we build against it. This is a small, new team standing up a new function. The playbook isn't written yet; we're writing it together.

About the Role

As our Digital Adoption & Lifecycle Manager, you'll own the communications that drive adoption, retention, and expansion across Mixpanel's customer base, with our digital-only customers as the sharpest test of whether the programs work. You'll design lifecycle programs triggered by real behavior: a team that just implemented but hasn't built their first report, an account whose query volume dropped for three straight weeks, a power user hitting the edge of their current plan. Then you'll write the emails and in-product messages that move them forward.

This is a builder's role, not a maintainer's role. You'll define the segmentation, write the copy, set up the triggers, instrument the measurement, and then argue with the data about what to change.

It's also a deeply collaborative one. You'll work hand in hand with our Customer Success Digital Programs Manager, sharing a roadmap and dividing the work. You'll partner with Marketing on the overall email calendar so our lifecycle sends and their campaigns aren't competing for the same inbox. You'll support adoption initiatives coming out of Product, turning a launch into something customers actually try. And you'll take cues from customer-facing teams about what's landing and what isn't. Very little of this job happens alone.

You'll also help define what agentic customer success looks like at Mixpanel. The scaled programs we build today are rules and triggers; the ones we build next will involve AI agents that can interpret a customer's situation, decide what that customer needs, and act. We're early here and we don't have the answers. We want someone who is already experimenting, who already has opinions about where agents help and where they break trust, and who wants to shape how this gets built.

If you like clean handoffs and finished systems, this isn't it. If you want to build the thing from zero and own the number it moves, read on.

Responsibilities

  • Build the lifecycle communication program end-to-end across onboarding, adoption, retention, and expansion, from strategy through copy, build, launch, and iteration

Headquarters: Remote Toronto, ON Canada | Remote United States

BeyondTrust is a place where you can bring your purpose to life through the work that you do, creating a safer world through our cybersecurity SaaS portfolio.

Our culture of flexibility, trust, and continual learning means you will be recognized for your growth and for the impact you make on our success. You will be surrounded by people who challenge, support, and inspire you to be the best version of yourself.

The Role

As a Senior Security Technical Program Manager at BeyondTrust, you will use your technical expertise, business acumen and security domain knowledge to manage and streamline critical CISO Office operations and programs. In this role, you will be an advocate for building seamless and metrics-driven operational frameworks. You will be responsible for working collaboratively with CISO Office teams and business stakeholders to identify operational gaps, document requirements and needs, metrics visualization, and execute programs to streamline the way BeyondTrust build and retains customer trust.

What You’ll Do

  • Oversee, plan, and manage security initiatives for all security pillars.
  • Serve as the Security TPM for the security issues management program, running the end-to-end lifecycle on the security issues management Jira board from identification and triage through handoff, validation, closure, and reporting.
  • Triage every new issues against the priority rubric (exploitability, blast radius, data sensitivity, regulatory or audit linkage, and compensating controls), confirm or adjust the Reporter’s initial priority, and set a due date at triage, hand off to Assignee as identified.
  • Own Critical and High issues day to day, including executive notification, direct engagement with the Assignee, unblocking dependencies, and fast-tracking validation. Monitor additional issues through the recurring security issues management review and step in when an escalation trigger fires.
  • Enforce the analysis gate before handoff, approving a ticket as handoff-ready only when root cause, a specific recommended remediation, named impacted systems and teams, and verifiable acceptance criteria are documented.
  • Identify the correct accountable Assignee by role, run a single structured handoff meeting, and drive formal acceptance in Jira within the agreed window.
  • Confirm Assignee remediation plans meet the acceptance criteria without redesigning them, and help surface cross-team dependencies such as budget, tooling, or other teams.
  • Run the recurring cross-functional security issues review, require an updated due date and logged reason for any slippage, and act as decision-maker on priority and acceptance-criteria disputes, escalating unresolved disagreements to the Sponsor.
  • Formally close security issues only after independent Security validation passes, and reopen failed validations to the Assignee with the specific gap noted.
  • Maintain security issues management board hygiene, including identifying duplicate or overlapping tickets, consolidation opportunities, and tickets missing descriptions, due dates, or owners.
  • Lead the Cloud Governance program to convert eligible cloud-scoped remediations into enforceable Kion guardrails.
  • Create detailed project plans to support each initiative while defining and supporting metric visualization for all of BT. 
  • Provide a steady stream of ideas and solutions during security initiatives to introduce innovation and improve operational efficiency. 
  • Implement relevant metrics to measure security specific program success, including the security issues management program health (open and closed volume by priority tier, overdue tickets, tickets not yet accepted, and due-date slippage).
  • Develop reports to communicate program progress, including the monthly rollup and the quarterly Sponsor program review, to leadership and cross-functional stakeholders. 
  • Collaborate with other cross-functional teams. 
  • Identify cross-team dependencies to incorporate them into the program planning process. 
  • Ensure root cause analysis is completed for technical issues and security findings, and shepherd the implementation of solutions through accountable owners. 
  • Make necessary recommendations for adjustments to security processes based on performance metrics. 
  • Influence strategic decisions about security direction.
  • Participates in building and managing of AI processes to create operational efficiency.
  • Ensure complete compliance according to industry standards by documenting all the processes and adjusting them, when necessary. 
  • Manage project escalations and help assemble project teams to tackle critical items, including executing the security issues

About Tailscale 

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

The Community Programs team creates the spaces, programs, and opportunities that help our community thrive. We're looking for a Community Engagement and Advocacy Manager to help us strengthen relationships with the people who use, build with, and advocate for Tailscale.

In this role, you'll own and grow three important areas of our community: the Tailscale Insiders advocacy program, our digital communities, specifically Discord and Reddit, and our Community Projects program.

You'll focus on creating meaningful opportunities for community members to connect, contribute, share their expertise, and be recognized for the work they do. Whether that's helping an Insider find their next speaking opportunity, bringing Tailscale staff into conversations on Discord, or showcasing an exciting community-built project, you'll help turn community participation into lasting relationships and advocacy.

You'll work closely with teams across Tailscale, including Developer Relations, Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Support, to connect community members with the right people, resources, and opportunities.

We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys working with people, understands what makes communities thrive, and can turn ideas into thoughtful, well-run programs. You don't need to be deeply technical, but you should be curious about technology and excited to learn from the people building with it.

  • Gather feedback from program members and continuously improve the Insider experience.
  • Track program participation, contributions, engagement, and outcomes to understand and communicate the impact of the program.

  • Develop and execute engagement initiatives, including community events, AMAs, discussions, and member spotlights that encourage participation and connection.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: Raleigh, North Carolina, USA; Remote, East Coast USA

Joining Collibra's Sales Compensation team

Collibra is the global leader in data intelligence, helping organizations find, understand, trust, and access data at scale.

You'll join the Sales Compensation team, which sits within Finance and works alongside Sales Operations and Total Rewards to design, calculate, and pay commissions for quota-carrying Collibrians across North America and EMEA. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Sales Compensation  you will be the hands-on owner of sales comp operations, plan logic in Xactly, monthly close, dispute resolution, and the annual plan cycle. Because every seller sees the output of this work each month, the team lives our value of being open, direct, and kind: we explain how a number was calculated, we say when something is wrong, and we fix it in the open.

This is a hybrid role based in our Raleigh office or remote US. Our hybrid model means you’ll work from the office at least two days each week. This setup helps us stay connected, work more closely together, and keep making progress as a team.

  • Administering incentive plan logic in our ICM platform, including quotas, rates, accelerators, SPIFFs, and overlay rules, and supporting rep data feeds from Salesforce and Workday, in order to keep the system aligned to approved plan documents.

  • Partnering with Accounting and FP&A on commission expense accruals, quarterly true-ups, and variance explanations, in order to support journal entries and a defensible close.
  • Making the function repeatable through SOPs, data maps and dictionaries, audit-ready documentation, and automation of manual workarounds, so that sales comp scales with the go-to-market organization.

  • 6+ years in an analytical role, with at least 4 years in a dedicated sales compensation function at a B2B SaaS or high-growth technology company.

  • Inclined to ask how a process can be made repeatable and scalable, including by applying AI and automation tools to routine comp work, rather than accepting manual workarounds.

jobs.title: Elation Health: Senior Manager, Commercial Learning and Development
jobs.description:
Headquarters: US - Remote

At Elation, our team is committed to enhancing physician and patient quality of life. We are a SaaS cloud-based clinical platform on a mission to enable every patient to receive the highest quality of care. Since inception, we’ve been focused on building a delightful, world‑class customer experience that empowers physicians to focus on delivering phenomenal care to patients.

Elation Health is looking for a Senior Manager, Training & Enablement to build and lead a dedicated function that strengthens how our employees and customers learn.

As Elation grows, we’re investing in a coordinated, scalable approach to training and education. You’ll lead a small, nimble team and own internal learning programs for Sales, Customer Success, Professional Services, Onboarding, Support, and other teams. You’ll also set the direction for customer education, partnering with customer-facing leaders to develop programs for new and existing customers.

This is a hands-on leadership role with the opportunity to shape the function’s strategy, programs, and ways of working. You’ll coach your team while staying directly involved in curriculum development, content creation, and training delivery.

This role reports to the Director of Product and Customer Marketing and works closely with leaders and subject matter experts across the organization.

What You’ll Do

Build and lead the function

  • Establish a training and enablement strategy aligned with company goals and functional priorities.
  • Lead needs analysis: identify performance gaps, determine where training will have the biggest impact, and prioritize from that analysis rather than primarily responding to requests for courses.
  • Evaluate existing programs and resources, identify opportunities to strengthen them, and develop a roadmap for growth.
  • Manage and develop a small team, setting clear priorities, responsibilities, and quality standards.
  • Establish consistent processes for training requests, program development, and content maintenance.

Develop and deliver internal learning programs

  • Own role-based onboarding and ongoing training for customer-facing teams, adapting content to each audience’s responsibilities.
  • Collaborate with commercial leaders to develop training that supports their commercial strategy and priorities.
  • Design and facilitate live and on-demand learning covering products, workflows, launches, and role-specific skills.
  • Partner with functional leaders and subject matter experts to translate complex information into clear, actionable instruction.
  • Reinforce learning after the session through hands-on practice, job aids, manager coaching resources, and train-the-trainer programs so new skills hold up on the job.

Expand customer education

  • Support the customer education strategy and roadmap, in partnership with the teams that deliver customer onboarding and training today, so priorities are clear and content is not duplicated.
  • Build a mix of live sessions and self-guided content tailored to different customer roles and experience levels, and set the standard for how customer education content is produced and kept current.
  • Use customer questions and feedback to keep education relevant as our products and customers’ needs evolve.

Improve how we work and measure success

  • Use AI to accelerate content development and program maintenance while maintaining accuracy and quality.
  • Develop tools and workflows that make learning resources easy to find, use, and keep current.
  • Measure behavior change, not just completion. Use learner feedback, assessments, on-the-job application, and business outcomes to show where learning is changing how people work and where it is not.

Priorities for the First 6-12 Months

This role spans strategy, people management, content development, and customer education. In the first year, the emphasis is on:

  • Establish a needs-driven approach. Assess existing programs and requests across customer-facing teams, identify the biggest performance gaps, and set priorities from that analysis rather than from the queue of course requests.
  • Rebuild onboarding for priority roles. Focus first on the highest-volume customer-facing roles, with practice, reinforcement, and manager coaching built in from the start.
  • Stand up the function. Build and develop the team, define how training requests are triaged and prioritized, and set quality and maintenance standards for content.
  • Set the customer education direction. Agree with customer-facing leaders on what this role owns versus what stay

About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is building the runtime control layer for the AI era, helping engineering teams govern what ships in production and how software and AI agents behave after deployment.

As Senior Accounting Manager, you’ll play a key role in strengthening the financial operations behind that work: owning critical close and technical accounting activities, supporting international entities and audit readiness, and partnering across Finance, Technology, and the business. You’ll also lead and develop a global team while improving accounting workflows, systems, and controls, including through automation and AI. This is an opportunity to combine hands-on accounting expertise with meaningful leadership and operational impact at a company shaping how teams build and run software.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing global accounting team with clear roles, decision rights, objectives, and development plans
  • Manage and accelerate close activities for key corporate accounting functions, including general accounting, treasury, accounts payable, employee reimbursements, and corporate card program management, and identify opportunities for close timeline compression
  • Prepare and review journal entries, balance sheet reconciliations, and variance analyses in compliance with US GAAP and internal accounting policies
  • Execute technical accounting for stock-based compensation (ASC 718), leases (ASC 842), and foreign currency matters (ASC 830), including drafting analyses and memos for review
  • Lead the implementation of a procure-to-pay (PTP) tool, with a focus on the PO-to-Pay workflow, partnering with Procurement, IT, and business stakeholders from requirements through rollout and adoption
  • Support and partner with the International Accounting team to ensure intercompany transactions and subsidiaries’ financial reporting are accurate and timely
  • Partner with Technology teams and business stakeholders on ERP enhancements/implementations, integrations, and reporting improvements
  • Document and maintain accounting policies, procedures, and key controls
  • Identify and implement opportunities for workflow improvement and systems optimization/AI automation across the close and accounting operations lifecycle

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting, finance, or a related field
  • At least eight years of progressive accounting experience
  • At least three years of experience leading a team of accountants
  • Strong knowledge of US GAAP
  • Hands-on experience in NetSuite (or a similar ERP), including improving workflows and reports
  • Ability to operate independently with strong accountability and initiative
  • Demonstrated experience using automation and AI tools to improve efficiency and accuracy in accounting operations
  • Experience working in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment
  • Ability to work across Finance and the business and explain complex accounting clearly to leaders, auditors, and colleagues outside Finance

  • Preferred, not required:

    • Big 4 experience
    • CPA certification
    • Experience in a high-growth technology company
